I am 65 years old and I have farmed my 8 mu of land in Quzhou County for over forty years. I only went to primary school, but I know this soil and this climate better than any book. My winter wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October right after the autumn rains, like I have done every year since I was young. Everyone in my village grows wheat followed by summer maize; it is the only system that makes sense here. My neighbor tried cotton five years ago and could barely sell it, so I stick to what I know. 

For the wheat, I bought improved seed from the agricultural supply shop — about 30 jin per mu. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and I will topdress with urea when the wheat turns green and again at jointing. I do not weigh every bag on a scale, but from the shop bags I figure it comes to about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu, maybe 8 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium. I would rather use a little too much than too little; I still remember 1997 when I tried to save money on fertilizer and the crop was thin and hungry. I will irrigate four times: once when the wheat wakes up in spring, once at jointing, once at heading, and once during grain filling. The tube well water costs money, but without it the wheat will burn up in May. I will spray pesticide four times — herbicide early, then insecticide and fungicide as needed. I ploughed before planting last fall with the rotary tiller. I expect about 450 kg per mu if the weather stays normal.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I have maybe two or three days to get the summer maize in the ground. There is no time for ploughing, so I plant no-till directly into the wheat stubble. I will buy hybrid seed — probably Nongda or something similar — about 1 package per mu. Maize is easier than wheat: I give it about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium, mostly compound fertilizer at planting and one urea topdressing when it is knee-high. I will irrigate twice, once right after planting if it is dry, and once at the big flare stage. Three pesticide sprays should be enough. If the summer rains come at the right time, I expect around 520 kg per mu of maize. That wheat plus maize double crop is my insurance — if one fails, the other usually carries us through.
